title: NGINX regex location beats an overlapping plain prefix (or is refused)
claims: an overlapping regex location keeps nginx precedence: /img/a.png goes to the regex backend
the plain prefix still serves non-matching paths under it
source_semantics: nginx location selection: exact '=' first, then longest plain prefix is remembered; unless it is '^~', regex locations are checked in config order and the first match wins. Ferrum ranks prefix above regex (docs/routing.md), so a naive translation would route /img/a.png to the prefix backend; that must be preserved or refused. Documentation-inferred unless the upstream differential runs.
